prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Desktop Controls Quick-Guide Screen Before Finish [finish, new_screen]: predicted +8.0%, measured -9.1% (p=0.127482), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Cloud Save Security Copy on Sign-In Screen [sign_in, copy]: predicted +5.0%, measured -4.0% (p=0.142096), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Photo Quality Hints for Custom Pet Upload [adoption, hint]: predicted +10.0%, measured -4.7% (p=0.287662), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Detailed Wait Progress & Time Estimate Indicator [home, wait_info]: predicted +7.0%, measured +0.4% (p=0.915657), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Move Sign-In After Adoption Certificate [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +4.0%, measured -1.7% (p=0.49003), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Split-Screen Companion Persona Selector [adoption, redesign]: predicted +3.0%, measured -9.4% (p=0.020458), lost: worse
- round 2: Desktop Controls Setup Checklist [finish, layout]: predicted +2.0%, measured +3.7% (p=0.522457), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Background Processing Desktop Alert System [home, notification]: predicted +2.0%, measured -6.9% (p=0.022894), lost: worse

Previous lessons:
Predictions were consistently too high across all tests, as none produced statistically significant improvements.
Adding new screens (such as desktop controls quick-guides before finish) showed no clear effect.
Updating sign-in copy with cloud save security details showed no clear effect.
Adding photo quality hints during adoption upload showed no clear effect.
Adding wait progress and time estimate indicators on the home screen showed no clear effect.

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Predictions were consistently too high across all tests, as no test produced statistically significant wins.
Split-screen redesigns for adoption persona selection significantly worsened performance.
Adding background processing desktop alert systems significantly worsened performance.
Adding new screens, photo quality hints, or wait progress indicators showed no clear effect.
Reordering sign-in steps, updating security copy, or adding setup checklists showed no clear effect.
